title: Chana chaat salad jar
summary: No cooking at all. Chickpeas, whatever is crunchy, lemon and chaat masala. Keeps four days and gets better after one.

ingredients.qty: 2 cups boiled, or 1 can drained and rinsed

ingredients.note: This is what makes it taste like chaat and not like a sad salad.

steps: Drain and rinse the chickpeas properly - the canning liquid tastes metallic.
Chop everything to roughly chickpea size so each spoonful gets a bit of each thing.
Toss it all together with the lemon, chaat masala, cumin and salt.
Taste and correct. It almost always needs more lemon and more salt than you think.
Eat now, or pack into jars: dressing at the bottom, chickpeas next, soft things, leaves on top. Shake when you eat.
tips: Add the cucumber and any leaves the morning you eat it if you are prepping ahead - they go limp by day two.
Cooking dry chana yourself is a third of the price of tins: soak overnight, pressure cook 15 minutes with salt.
Add 100 g of crumbled paneer or a chopped boiled egg and it becomes a proper meal rather than a side.
health_notes: 12 g of fibre a serving, which is close to half a day's worth. Chickpeas are low-GI, so this does not spike the way a sandwich lunch does.

source.adapted: Street chana chaat, without the fried sev and sweet chutney.
